title: Pinning SLA Mitigation Briefing
summary: Working briefing on how strict regional pinning affects availability, latency, and cost for Private and Dedicated customers, plus prioritized mitigations and operational controls.
scope: Private deployments (VPC, on-prem) and Dedicated clusters with explicit region/zone pinning
Customer requests that restrict cross-region inference or limit fallback options
Interactions with autoscaling, reserved capacity, and burst pools
quick_takeaways: Hard region pinning raises SLA exposure by reducing available failover capacity
Local warm pools and proactive capacity reservation are the most reliable mitigations
Offer contractual pinning tiers (soft, hybrid, hard) with different SLAs and pricing
Current telemetry gaps (per-route headroom) prevent confident SLA guarantees — fix this first
sla_impact_matrix: Normal demand: latency targets met if local capacity >= 2x expected peak; otherwise p95 degrades
In-region AZ failure: multi-AZ warm replicas mitigate impact but single-AZ setups risk <99.5% availability
Region-wide outage: without approved secondary region, availability equals region pool availability and customer-visible errors increase
Network egress limits: pinning can increase intra-region network pressure and queueing, raising tail latency
mitigation_patterns: Reserved warm capacity: keep 20-40% headroom in pinned region (recommended for latency SLOs)
Soft canary fallback: allow routing to an approved secondary region within same legal boundary with audit logging
Hybrid pin control plane only: control plane pinned but execution allowed in approved additional zones under contract
Aggressive batching + KV prefix caching: reduces compute load at the cost of slightly higher p50 for small requests
Edge-affine prewarming: small replicas in each AZ to reduce tail during AZ failover
Customer-side agreed backpressure: retry-after headers and max-inflight to preserve p90 during stress
operational_playbook: Console defaults: suggest minimum reserved commit based on 95th percentile qPS; surface pinning tier and recommended headroom
Alerting: sustained headroom <15% for >10 minutes -> page SRE + notify SE

Incident steps: 1) confirm AZ vs region outage; 2) if AZ-only, shift to warm AZ replicas; 3) if region and soft-fallback allowed, enable approved secondary; 4) if hard-pin, open customer escalation and enable throttles
Post-incident: publish timeline, capacity headroom logs, customer comms, and lessons learned
cost_vs_reliability_options: Option A (low cost): no reserved capacity, Basic SLA, higher incident risk
Option B (balanced): 6-12 month reserved capacity at 1.5x baseline qPS, target 99.9% regional availability
Option C (high reliability): dedicated pinned cluster with multi-AZ redundancy + contractual approved hot spare region (if legal OK)
telemetry_checklist: Alerts to add: sustained headroom <15% for >10m, region_error_rate >1% for 5m
Customer dashboard: expose SLI (availability, p50/p95) and headroom
testing_plan: Chaos: simulate AZ failover while pinned and measure p50/p95 and error rates
Load: synthetic bursts with different batching and cache configs to quantify token cost vs latency
Durability: 72-hour mirrored traffic test under pinned constraints for contractual proof
open_questions: Acceptable legal language for "approved secondary region" — legal to supply template
Default recommended headroom % per instance class — engineering to finalize
Billing for soft-fallback events — should rates change when traffic runs in approved secondary region?
